FROMLIST: Bluetooth: btusb: request wake pin with NOAUTOEN Badly-designed systems might have (for example) active-high wake pins that default to high (e.g., because of external pull ups) until they have an active firmware which starts driving it low. This can cause an interrupt storm in the time between request_irq() and disable_irq(). We don't support shared interrupts here, so let's just pre-configure the interrupt to avoid auto-enabling it. vm_tools: maitred: max stateful fs size at boot As a first step toward more dynamic stateful disk sizing, add a btrfs online resize operation to maximize the filesystem within its block device. This will take place on each boot, but it should have minimal overhead if the block device size has not changed (less than 10 ms) and should not take a significant amount of time even when actually resizing, since this will always be expanding into new free space, which doesn't require any shuffling of existing data (growing a 1 GB FS to 2 GB takes less than 100 ms on my test system). Note that this will only work for expanding the disk image; it is not safe to shrink the disk image unless the filesystem is shrunk first, which will never happen in this code path due to the use of 'max' as the size specifier. The approach taken here is enough to allow the virtual block device image to be resized to let the VM consume newly-available free space that wasn't available at VM creation time. Shrinking the VM disk image would need to issue a BTRFS resize operation with an absolute size specified, followed by shrinking the disk image file to that size. However, since we use a sparse backing file for the stateful disk image, free space should already be reclaimed from the VM even if the logical disk size is larger than the available space. Tested by manually expanding the stateful disk image with truncate(1) and restarting the VM, observing the change in filesystem size. debugd: Have log_tool read file logs directly log_tool aggregates logs from many different sources. The logs are specified as the output of running a shell command. However, often this shell command is just running cat on some file. There is no need to start another process just to read a file from disk. This change adds two different log types to log_tool: file logs, and command logs. Command logs are the same as before; the output of a shell command. File logs instead just specify a path, and that path is read directly from C++. The process effective uid and effective gid are set before the reads so that file permissions are respected. Additionally, this change splits a couple of log entries that were the combined output of two files into two different log entries. Performance testing over 5 trials showed a .6 second improvement in response time for log_tool when calling GetAllLogs.
